title: Marcos defends economic team
summary: President Marcos defended on Friday members of his economic team against criticisms amid slowing growth, rising inflation and a weakening peso.

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. answers questions from members of the media during Kapihan with the Media in Shenzhen, China on November 20, 2026
MANILA, Philippines — President Marcos defended on Friday members of his economic team against criticisms amid slowing growth, rising inflation and a weakening peso.
Sen. Panfilo Lacson earlier urged Marcos to reconsider his economic team in light of the performance of the economy.

“No, I don’t… I disagree with him, I’m sorry, but I disagree with him. All the difficulties we’re going through can be clearly directly traced to the war in Iran,” the President said at a press conference in Shenzhen, China.

He also clarified that the recent movements in the Cabinet – with barely two years left in the administration – were part of the administration’s response to the events that are happening around the world.
Marcos said shifting one Cabinet member to another position does not produce instability.
“I know people talk about shuffle. It’s not a shuffle, it’s putting people in the place… There are very specific reasons for them,” he said.
“There’s no general reason that I’m not happy with the Cabinet or anything like that. No, not at all. Quite the contrary,” Marcos said.

“We’re trying to put the best people to the best use, because issues come up that didn’t exist before in certain departments. So, we’re trying to put the people who are best able to address those issues into the proper department,” he said.
Transportation Secretary Giovanni Lopez and Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon recently swapped posts.

The administration also carried out leadership shake-ups in the Bureau of Customs (BOC), Bureau of Internal Revenue, Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) and the Bases Conversion and Development Authority.
The Philippine Exporters Confederation Inc. earlier expressed concern over the leadership changes, particularly at PEZA and BOC.
